evidence.positive: Against the running mayo-mayo tenant at localhost:60083 (image loop-100ab1bd9), boot logged 'Saved 463 antibiotic pathways for tenant TenantKey[value=mayo-mayo]; table holds 463'. A SQL reconstruction of "mayo-mayo".antibiotic_pathways/_options/_option_medication_categories showed all 17 procedures the ticket names carrying exactly the two pathways it specifies: the 3 GI procedures (p-duodenal-ulcer, p-exploratory-laparotomy, p-exploratory-laparoscopy) at pathway 0 '(CEFAZOLIN) -> (VANCOMYCIN)' and pathway 1 '(CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) OR (CIPROFLOXACIN AND CLINDAMYCIN)'; the 14 gyn/urogyn procedures (p-myomectomy-open/-laparoscopic/-robotic, p-pelvic-floor-repair-open/-laparoscopic/-robotic/-endoscopic, p-urogynecologic-with-cystoscopy-other, p-urogynecologic-no-cystoscopy-other, p-gynecologic-laparoscopic-other, p-gynecologic-open-other, p-vulvectomy, p-vesicovaginal-fistula, p-rectovaginal-fistula) at pathway 0 '(CEFAZOLIN) -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND VANCOMYCIN)' and pathway 1 '(CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND VANCOMYCIN AND METRONIDAZOLE)'. Each of the 17 was then exercised at runtime: a mayo-mayo patient and case were created per procedure through POST /api/admin/patients/ and /operations/create, and the walk read back from GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates (which drops the cached resolution and re-walks). 34 scenarios, 0 failures. With no allergy every procedure returned outcome=RECOMMENDED offering [CEFAZOLIN] and [CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE] with both step-1 options marked RECOMMENDED. With a cefazolin allergy added (POST /allergies?type=ALLERGEN&identifier=a-cefazolin), contraindicated=["CEFAZOLIN"] and each route fell to its own fallback: the GI set returned RECOMMENDED [VANCOMYCIN], [CIPROFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE], [CIPROFLOXACIN, CLINDAMYCIN]; the gyn set returned RECOMMENDED [CIPROFLOXACIN, VANCOMYCIN] and [CIPROFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE, VANCOMYCIN].
evidence.negative: Procedures the ticket does not name were driven through the same endpoint and did not pick up these pathways. p-hysterectomy-open (the adjacent gyn set) carried a single pathway 'CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE -> CIPROFLOXACIN AND VANCOMYCIN AND METRONIDAZOLE': no allergy gave RECOMMENDED [[CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE]] only - the bare-CEFAZOLIN route the 14 gyn procedures get was absent - and with a cefazolin allergy it gave RECOMMENDED [[CIPROFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE, VANCOMYCIN]] only, never the metronidazole-free [CIPROFLOXACIN, VANCOMYCIN]. p-duodenectomy (name-adjacent GI, sits in the biliary/GI block) carried only 'CEFAZOLIN -> CIPROFLOXACIN' and returned [[CEFAZOLIN]] then [[CIPROFLOXACIN]] - neither VANCOMYCIN nor the cipro+metronidazole/cipro+clindamycin combos appeared. p-cholecystectomy returned its own 'CEFAZOLIN -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) OR (CIPROFLOXACIN AND CLINDAMYCIN)' with no VANCOMYCIN. p-colonoscopy resolved NO_PROPHYLAXIS_INDICATED with recommended=[]. Scope was also checked at the tenant level: none of these 17 procedure identifiers exist in the demo or mgb procedure catalogs (0 rows in "demo-demo".procedure_types), so Mayo is the only tenant that can carry them.
evidence.red_check: The shipped bundled CSV was copied out of the container (/app/resources/data/org/mayo/procedures/antibiotic-pathways.csv, md5 431c6f703ec46c85cbfa339a1d6d9749, byte-identical to the worktree source), backed up in-container to /tmp, and replaced with a two-line flip: (a) the GI pathway-0 row reverted to the pre-update literal 'CEFAZOLIN' with no VANCOMYCIN fallback, and (b) p-hysterectomy-open appended to the gyn pathway-0 row's procedure list. After a container restart the importer logged 'Saved 464 antibiotic pathways' (up from 463) and both checks went red. Positive red: p-duodenal-ulcer and p-exploratory-laparotomy with a cefazolin allergy flipped from RECOMMENDED with three regimens to outcome=ALL_CONTRAINDICATED, recommended=[], and the log emitted 'Procedure p-duodenal-ulcer recommends nothing: 1 of its 2 pathways survived no option' - a line that appears zero times in the pre-flip log. Negative red: p-hysterectomy-open began offering [[CEFAZOLIN], [CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE]] with no allergy and [[CIPROFLOXACIN, VANCOMYCIN], [CIPROFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE, VANCOMYCIN]] with the allergy - exactly the regimens the shipped config reserves for the 14 named procedures. The shipped CSV was then restored and the container restarted; md5 of the in-container file matched the /tmp backup and the extracted original (431c6f703ec46c85cbfa339a1d6d9749), the importer logged 'Saved 463 antibiotic pathways' again, p-hysterectomy-open returned to its single metronidazole route, the duodenal-ulcer allergic case returned to RECOMMENDED [VANCOMYCIN]/[CIPROFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE]/[CIPROFLOXACIN, CLINDAMYCIN], and the full 34-scenario batch re-ran with 0 failures.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway build of main (100ab1bd9) on the mayo-mayo tenant.

Positive: the bundled Mayo antibiotic-pathways config imports all 17 procedures this ticket names with exactly the two pathways specified, and every one of them was driven through a real case. With no allergy each offered CEFAZOLIN and CEFAZOLIN plus METRONIDAZOLE; with a cefazolin allergy each route fell to its own fallback - the GI set to VANCOMYCIN, CIPROFLOXACIN plus METRONIDAZOLE and CIPROFLOXACIN plus CLINDAMYCIN, the gyn set to CIPROFLOXACIN plus VANCOMYCIN and CIPROFLOXACIN plus VANCOMYCIN plus METRONIDAZOLE. 34 scenarios, no failures.

Negative: procedures not named here did not pick up these pathways. p-hysterectomy-open carried only its metronidazole route and never offered bare CEFAZOLIN or the metronidazole-free CIPROFLOXACIN plus VANCOMYCIN; p-duodenectomy stayed on CEFAZOLIN falling to CIPROFLOXACIN; p-colonoscopy resolved to no prophylaxis indicated. None of these procedure identifiers exist in the demo or MGB catalogs, so Mayo is the only tenant that can carry them.

Red check: the bundled CSV in the running container was flipped two ways - the duodenal-ulcer route reverted to the pre-update bare CEFAZOLIN, and p-hysterectomy-open added to the gyn bare-CEFAZOLIN route. On restart both checks went red: the allergic duodenal-ulcer case became ALL_CONTRAINDICATED with no guidance at all, and p-hysterectomy-open began offering the regimens reserved for the 14 named procedures. The shipped file was restored, the checksum re-verified, and every observation returned to green.

One note for the record: the shipped duodenal-ulcer pathway 1 is CEFAZOLIN falling to VANCOMYCIN, not the bare CEFAZOLIN written in this ticket. The fallback was added afterwards, and the red check shows why - without it a cefazolin-allergic case gets no recommendation at all.

Automation: existing coverage asserts both pathway shapes against the real bundled file, but samples only 6 of the 17 procedures and has no inverse assertion. Proposed follow-up:

- extend the importer test to all 14 gyn/urogyn identifiers
- assert the p-hysterectomy set carries only the metronidazole route
- add a resolution test walking the real bundled config for the allergic duodenal-ulcer case
